findings.who: A filer bought a car in 2023 for personal use and began using it in a business in 2025. The IRS treats the car as placed in service on the date of conversion.
findings.why_no: Read without help, "Placed in service in 2025" sounds like "bought or first driven in 2025". The filer answers no because they have owned and driven the car since 2023. The gate is then false, and neither used_before nor bonus_excluded is asked. This harms the gated lines only if some other path still gives the vehicle a 2025 special allowance. Otherwise the error is the lost allowance and the wrong recovery start, which are outside these gated lines.
findings.irs_text: i4562 p.14, Column (b): "If property held for personal use is converted to business/investment use, treat the property as placed in service on the date of conversion." p463 p.25: "if you first start using the car only for personal use and later convert it to business use, you place the car in service on the date of conversion."
findings.fix: Add help to the placed-in-service helper: "Answer yes if you first started using this vehicle for business or investment in 2025, even if you bought it earlier for personal use."

findings.who: A filer has a business car placed in service in 2022 and made a major improvement to it in 2025, such as a new engine. The improvement is a new item of 5-year property placed in service in 2025, and a special allowance may be claimed on it.
findings.why_no: The question asks about "this vehicle", and the vehicle was placed in service in 2022, so the filer answers no. The improvement's own 2025 placement in service and its allowance are never routed through the gate. If the tool computes an allowance for the improvement elsewhere, the original-use and 168(k)(9) checks are skipped for that allowance.
findings.irs_text: p463 p.26: "A major improvement to a car is treated as a new item of 5-year recovery property. It is treated as placed in service in the year the improvement is made... you must treat the improvement and the car as a whole when applying the limits"
findings.fix: Either gate on "the vehicle or a major improvement to it was placed in service in 2025 and a special allowance is claimed", or ask separately about 2025 improvements and apply the same eligibility questions to them.

findings.who: A filer placed a qualifying business vehicle in service in 2025 and did not attach an election-out statement, so the special allowance applies by default. The filer does not think of themselves as "claiming" anything.
findings.why_no: "A special allowance is claimed" reads like an affirmative choice. A filer who made no choice answers no. This is harmless if the tool then computes no allowance for the vehicle. If the tool applies the default allowance anyway, the original-use and 168(k)(9) exclusions are never tested.
findings.irs_text: i4562 p.7, Exceptions: "Property for which you elected not to claim any special depreciation allowance"; Election out: "attach a statement to your timely filed return... indicating the class of property for which you are making the election"
findings.fix: Make sure the gate's "claimed" helper is the same flag that drives the allowance computation. Word the question as "Are you electing NOT to take the special depreciation allowance for this vehicle's class?" and derive "claimed" from its complement.

findings.who: A sole proprietor is the only driver of the car. It is driven 35% for the business and 30% for managing rental properties or other investments. No one else drives it and none of its use is entertainment.
findings.why_no: The gate asks only whether anyone else uses the car or whether any use is entertainment. Investment use by the filer is neither, so the truthful answer is no. Yet investment use is one of the uses the gated question removes from qualified business use.
findings.irs_text: i4562 p. 14, Lines 26 and 27: "a qualified business use is any use in your trade or business. However, it does not include any of the following. • Investment use."; p463 p. 25: "It doesn't include use for the production of income (investment use)"
findings.fix: Add investment use to the gate: "...or do you use any of it for investment or the production of income (not your trade or business)?" Better, always ask qbu_low whenever business/investment use is entered and includes any investment use.

findings.who: A filer regularly in the business of leasing cars, or one who bought this car to lease. At year end, or at the time they answer, the car sits in the fleet between leases or before its first lease, and no lessee has it.
findings.why_no: "Does anyone but you use this vehicle" is in the present tense and asks about actual use. A car that is held for lease but idle is truthfully used by no one else.
findings.irs_text: i4562 p. 15: "The business use requirement and the limits for passenger automobiles generally do not apply to passenger automobiles leased or held by anyone regularly engaged in the business of leasing passenger automobiles."
findings.fix: Add to the gate: "or do you hold it for lease, or are you in the business of leasing cars?" State that the question covers any time during the tax year.

findings.who: A filer leased or lent the car during part of the year and has it back now. The car went to a relative, to a 5% owner of the business, or to a government agency under a lease of 6 months or more. Another case: an employee had the car as a fringe benefit until leaving in June.
findings.why_no: The question uses the present tense ("Does anyone ... use", "someone you lease or lend it to"). A filer answering in the following spring describes current use and says no.
findings.irs_text: p946 p. 17: "you cannot elect the section 179 deduction for ... Certain property you lease to others (if you are a non-corporate lessor) ... Property used by governmental units or foreign persons or entities, except property used under a lease with a term of less than 6 months."
findings.fix: Reword: "At any time during the tax year, did anyone but you use this vehicle ...?"

findings.who: A married couple files jointly, and the car is used in one spouse's sole proprietorship. The other spouse works in the business and has the car as part of their pay, or the car is leased to the spouse's separate business.
findings.why_no: On a joint return the filer may read "you" as both spouses. Then the spouse is not "anyone but you", and "a relative" seems to mean other relatives.
findings.irs_text: i4562 p. 14: qualified business use does not include "Leasing the property to a 5% owner or related person ..." or "The use of the property as compensation for services performed by a 5% owner or related person."
findings.fix: Say explicitly: "Does anyone other than the owner — including your spouse — use this vehicle ..."

findings.who: A business owner uses the car for recreation or amusement with clients, such as driving them to a ski weekend or a golf trip. Another business owner uses it for other travel that section 274 makes nondeductible, such as a spouse's travel on a business trip.
findings.why_no: "Entertainment" reads as shows or parties. The filer does not see recreation, amusement, or other section 274 disallowed travel as "entertainment" and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i4562 p. 14: qualified business use does not include "The use of property that is determined to be non-deductible under section 274."
findings.fix: Reword: "or is any of its use for entertainment, recreation, or amusement, or other travel you cannot deduct (such as a spouse's or guest's trips)?"

findings.who: A sole proprietor placed a qualifying car in service in 2023 and never claimed bonus depreciation on it. They also never attached an election-out statement, so the special allowance was allowable even though it was not taken.
findings.why_no: The question asks 'Did you claim a special ('bonus') depreciation allowance'. They did not claim it, so they truthfully answer no. The IRS text, however, treats the allowance as taken unless the filer elected out.
findings.irs_text: i4562 p. 13, MACRS recapture: depreciation includes 'Any special depreciation allowance available for the property (unless you elected not to claim it)'; p946 p. 63: 'you would still reduce your basis by the maximum amount allowable'
findings.fix: Ask: 'Was a special (bonus) depreciation allowance claimed for this vehicle in an earlier year, or was it available and you did not attach a statement electing out of it for that year?' Add help explaining that the allowance counts unless an election-out statement was filed.

findings.who: A married couple files jointly. Before the marriage, or on an earlier separate return, the spouse placed the vehicle in service and either claimed bonus depreciation or used the standard mileage rate for it. The filer answering never did either.
findings.why_no: Each question says 'Did you claim…' or 'Did you use the standard mileage rate…'. The filer reads 'you' as themselves alone and truthfully answers no.
findings.irs_text: p463 p. 25, Exception: 'If you used the standard mileage rate in the first year of business use and change to the actual expenses method in a later year, you can't depreciate your car under the MACRS rules.'
findings.fix: Ask 'Did you, your spouse, or anyone else on a return for this vehicle claim…' or 'use the standard mileage rate for it in an earlier year?'

findings.who: A filer drove the car about 30% for their business and about 30% for an investment or rental activity in an earlier year. Commuting miles were also mixed in with the business miles.
findings.why_no: The question asks whether 'half or less of its use [was] for business'. The filer combines business and investment miles, or counts commuting, gets more than half, and answers no. Qualified business use excludes investment use, and commuting is not business use.
findings.irs_text: i4562 p. 14, Qualified business use: 'it does not include any of the following. • Investment use.'; p463 p. 25: 'It doesn't include use for the production of income (investment use)'
findings.fix: Ask about trade-or-business miles only, 'not counting investment use, commuting, or use by a 5% owner or related person as compensation', and add this to the help text.

findings.who: A filer bought a car for personal use in 2016 and converted it to business use in 2025. They enter the 2016 purchase date as the vehicle's date.
findings.why_no: The gate is computed from the recovery year. If that comes from the original purchase date rather than the conversion date, the gate reads 'not placed in service in 2025'. The tool then never asks 'Did you get it before September 28, 2017?', and the vehicle can wrongly receive the 2025 bonus allowance and the $20,200 limit. It also gets the prior-year questions instead.
findings.irs_text: i4562 p. 14, Column (b): 'If property held for personal use is converted to business/investment use, treat the property as placed in service on the date of conversion.'; i4562 p. 6: qualified property must be 'acquired after September 27, 2017'
findings.fix: Compute the recovery year from the business-use conversion date, and ask for that date explicitly. Ask the acquisition-date question whenever the conversion date falls in 2025, whatever the purchase date.

findings.who: A filer signed a written binding contract for a vehicle before September 28, 2017 and took delivery later. They placed it in service in 2025.
findings.why_no: 'Did you get it before September 28, 2017?' reads as taking delivery, so they answer no. Under a pre-date binding contract, the vehicle is treated as acquired before that date.
findings.irs_text: i4562 p. 7, Exceptions: 'Property described in section 168(k)(9)(A) or 168(k)(9)(B)'; p. 5: 'certain qualified property acquired after September 27, 2017'
findings.fix: Ask: 'Did you get it, or sign a binding contract to buy it, before September 28, 2017?'

findings.who: A joint filer now uses the family car in a Schedule C business. In an earlier year, the spouse placed the car in service in the spouse's own business and deducted actual expenses (depreciation or section 179).
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether 'you have used' the standard mileage rate 'every year you have used it for the business'. The filer has used only the mileage rate personally, in this business, so they answer Yes. The question is never asked, and the eligibility path treats the vehicle as always on the standard mileage rate. The question about the first year placed in service is skipped. The wrong answer here is a Yes to the parent, not a No.
findings.line: scveh.smr_first_if_not_always (with the eligibility for the standard mileage rate that it feeds)
findings.irs_text: i1040sc (2025) p. 6, Line 9: 'You can take the standard mileage rate for 2025 only if you: • Owned the vehicle and used the standard mileage rate for the first year you placed the vehicle in service'
findings.fix: Ask: 'Has anyone (you, your spouse, or a business of either of you) ever deducted actual expenses (gas, repairs, depreciation, section 179, or lease payments) for this vehicle in any year?' Change the help to say 'any business, not only this one'.

findings.who: A sole proprietor bought the car in 2022 and used it for business that year. They claimed depreciation and actual costs as an employee on an earlier return, or in a business they have since closed. They began this Schedule C business in 2024 and have used the mileage rate here since.
findings.why_no: 'Every year you have used it for the business' reads as 'this business'. The help's 'any earlier year' does not say 'in any business or job'. So the filer answers Yes, skips the first-year question, and claims the standard mileage rate, which the first year placed in service does not allow.
findings.irs_text: i1040sc (2025) p. 6, Line 9: 'used the standard mileage rate for the first year you placed the vehicle in service'
findings.fix: Tie the gate to the first year the vehicle was placed in service for any business or employment use: 'In the first year this vehicle was used for any business or job, did you (or your spouse) use the standard mileage rate rather than actual expenses?'

findings.who: A filer in the vehicle's first business year took no vehicle deduction at all, because they did not file or omitted it. Later they used the mileage rate.
findings.why_no: They did not use actual expenses, so the help points them to Yes. They may also answer No because they did not 'use' the mileage rate that year. Either way the instructions do not resolve whether they 'used the standard mileage rate for the first year'.
findings.irs_text: i1040sc (2025) p. 6, Line 9: 'Owned the vehicle and used the standard mileage rate for the first year you placed the vehicle in service'
findings.fix: Add help for a first year with no vehicle deduction claimed, and route it to the same treatment the tool adopts for the first-year rule.

findings.who: A fleet operator always used the mileage rate for this vehicle, but in 2025 used five or more vehicles simultaneously in the business.
findings.why_no: The gate cites the five-vehicle rule but asks only about past method. A truthful Yes skips the gated question, and nothing here applies the fleet bar.
findings.irs_text: i1040sc (2025) p. 6, Line 9: 'You must use actual expenses if you used five or more vehicles simultaneously in your business (such as in fleet operations).'
findings.fix: Confirm the five-or-more-vehicles bar is asked separately for each vehicle and overrides both paths. Otherwise add it to this gate.
